pool_saturation: Database connection pool saturation causes request queuing

hypothesis.title: Database connection pool saturation causes request queuing
hypothesis.explanation: The pool max_size is 20 (db.py) but the load test runs 200 concurrent users at ~300 req/s. App CPU is high (76-86%) while DB CPU is low (11-12%), indicating the app spends cycles waiting for a connection rather than executing queries. The low p50 (2.5 ms) shows queries are fast when a connection is available; the high p99 (2000+ ms) matches queuing delay for a pooled connection.
supporting_evidence: p50=2.5 ms vs p99=2000+ ms (queueing pattern)
missing_evidence: Direct measurement of pool wait time or queue depth

proposed_experiment.rationale: If pool saturation is the cause, raising the pool ceiling should eliminate queuing and collapse p99. If p99 stays high, the bottleneck is elsewhere.

predictions.if_supported: Pool saturation confirmed; p99 meets SLO.
predictions.if_refuted: Pool saturation disproved; p99 remains >50 ms despite larger pool.

events.message: eventloop_blocking: Synchronous PBKDF2 (200k iterations) blocks the event loop, delaying all requests

hypothesis.title: Synchronous PBKDF2 (200k iterations) blocks the event loop, delaying all requests
hypothesis.explanation: auth.hash_password and auth.verify_password run 200,000 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 iterations synchronously on the event loop (auth.py). The load test exercises login/register endpoints that call these functions. telemetry.monitor_event_loop records 'eventloop.lag' spans. High app CPU (86%) with low DB CPU suggests CPU-bound work in the event loop. If lag spikes correlate with request p99, the hashing is starving /me of event-loop time.
supporting_evidence: app CPU up to 86% while DB idle
contradicting_evidence: /me endpoint does not call password hashing directly

proposed_experiment.rationale: If event-loop blocking drives the tail, the 'eventloop.lag' span p99 will be high (hundreds of ms) and correlate with 'http GET /me' p99. If lag is low, the event loop is not the culprit.

predictions.if_supported: Event-loop blocking confirmed; offloading or reducing iterations should fix p99.
predictions.if_refuted: Event-loop blocking disproved; lag and hash spans are low, so hashing is not delaying /me.

events.message: unnecessary_column_fetch: Fetching unused password_hash column in /me query adds serialization and network overhead

hypothesis.title: Fetching unused password_hash column in /me query adds serialization and network overhead
hypothesis.explanation: current_user() selects u.password_hash (a ~100-char TEXT) but /me response only returns id, username, display_name. The extra column increases row size, PostgreSQL serialization, network transfer, and asyncpg parsing per request. Under high concurrency this per-request tax could widen the latency tail. DB CPU is low, but per-row overhead may not show as CPU.
supporting_evidence: Query selects password_hash but response omits it
p50 is low (2.5 ms) but tail is heavy (queueing amplifies per-request cost)
contradicting_evidence: Single column unlikely to add 2000 ms
missing_evidence: Per-query latency breakdown (network vs parse vs execute)

proposed_experiment.rationale: If the extra column materially contributes to the tail, removing it from the SELECT will reduce 'http GET /me' p99 measurably. If p99 is unchanged, the column is not a factor.

predictions.observation: app_spans['http GET /me'].p99_ms drops by >30% and db_activity.wait_events show reduced 'ClientRead'/'DataFileRead' time
predictions.if_supported: Column fetch contributes to tail; projection fix helps.
predictions.if_refuted: Column fetch disproved as significant factor; p99 unchanged.

key_observations: Baseline GET /me p99 across three runs: 2601.4 ms, 2087.5 ms, 2604.1 ms (avg ~2431 ms). After removing password_hash column, measured GET /me p99 = 2107.4 ms — a ~13% reduction, well below the predicted >30% drop if the column were a significant tail contributor.
Database wait events unchanged: only Client:ClientRead x1 observed, no reduction in ClientRead or DataFileRead time.

Overall GET /me p99 (2107.4 ms) remains far above the 50 ms SLO target, and other spans (POST /login p99 4209.3 ms, eventloop.lag p99 81.0 ms, auth.verify_password p99 58.6 ms) indicate the tail latency is dominated by other factors.
The small reduction falls within baseline run-to-run variance (2087.5 ms in one baseline run), so the change is not statistically distinguishable from noise.
conclusion.explanation: The hypothesis predicted that removing the unused password_hash column would cut GET /me p99 by >30% and reduce database read wait events. The measured p99 dropped only ~13% (within baseline variance) and wait events were identical. Therefore the column fetch is not a significant factor in the SLO violation.

events.message: eventloop_saturation_pbkdf2: Event loop saturation from synchronous PBKDF2 causes request queueing

hypothesis.title: Event loop saturation from synchronous PBKDF2 causes request queueing
hypothesis.explanation: The event loop is saturated with CPU-bound PBKDF2 work (200k iterations) from /login and /register endpoints. GET /me requests spend most of their tail latency queued in the event loop behind these CPU-bound tasks. The eventloop.lag span (p99 ~74-81ms) only measures timer wakeup latency, not queue depth. At 200 concurrent users with 200k PBKDF2 iterations, the event loop is saturated with CPU work (app CPU 76-86%), causing /me requests to queue for seconds. auth.verify_password p99 is only 53-59ms and eventloop.lag p99 is 74-81ms, but GET /me p99 is 2100-2600ms, indicating queueing delay dominates.
supporting_evidence: GET /me p99 consistently 2100-2600ms across runs while individual spans (auth.verify_password p99 53-59ms, eventloop.lag p99 74-81ms) are an order of magnitude smaller
POST /login p99 3700-4200ms indicates heavy PBKDF2 work in login endpoint
App CPU 76-86% at 200 concurrent users indicates CPU saturation
Database shows minimal activity (0.07 avg active connections, only ClientRead wait event), ruling out DB contention
Previous column-removal experiment reduced GET /me p99 only ~13% (within noise), confirming column fetch is not the tail driver
eventloop.lag p99 (74-81ms) << GET /me p99 (2100+ms) proves event loop timer latency is not the bottleneck; queue depth is
contradicting_evidence: eventloop_blocking hypothesis was DISPROVED (90%) because eventloop.lag p99 < 100ms threshold
auth.verify_password p99 53-59ms alone cannot explain 2100ms tail
missing_evidence: Direct measurement of event loop queue depth or task wait time
Behavior at lower concurrency or reduced PBKDF2 iterations

proposed_experiment.rationale: Reduce PBKDF2 iterations 10x (200k -> 20k) to drastically reduce CPU time per hash operation. If event loop saturation from PBKDF2 is the cause, /me p99 should drop proportionally (10x+). If not, tail latency persists.
